canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.black (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface) to gray.700, one step lighter than the reverted bg.surface (gray.800) — an intentional inversion of the usual dark-mode elevation cue (raised content is normally lighter than the canvas behind it), confirmed at explicit direction given canvas's narrower Storybook-specific usage. text.primary is fine at 6.59:1. text.secondary originally measured 4.00:1 here (failed the 4.5:1 AA text floor) — fixed the same day (2026-08-08) by moving text.secondary itself to gray.200, which measures 5.10:1 against this token (see text.secondary's own description); this note was left stale describing the pre-fix failure until corrected 2026-09-03. text.tertiary still measures 2.96:1 (fails even the 3:1 non-text floor) — no fix landed for it, and light mode fails too (4.13:1, found 2026-09-03 — see that theme's own description). Don't place text.tertiary literal text directly on bg.canvas, light or dark.

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision. Reordered (2026-08-20) to sit right after bg.canvas, per explicit direction — no value change.

scrim.$description: New token (2026-08-25, CloseButton review) — dark-mode value revised same day, at explicit direction, from neutral.white (this token's original, shared-across-all-4-themes value) to gray.800, the same step bg.surface itself resolved to in dark mode at the time. Moved again to gray.900 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), continuing to track bg.surface's own value — that token moved to gray.900 in the same coordinated darker-dark-mode pass (see its own description), and this one follows for the identical reason as before: a grounding layer should read as native to whatever the current dark surface actually is, not fixed to a value that could drift out of sync. A plain white scrim would sit inconsistently bright against a dark-themed app even though what it's grounding against (unpredictable external content) is by design outside this system's control. No fixed WCAG contrast pairing is possible here, since what this composites over is arbitrary, unlike every other bg.* / text.* pairing in this file. Opacity is applied separately, compositionally, at the component layer (CloseButton.module.css, opacity.40) rather than baked into this token. Positioned directly after bg.overlay — both are opacity-composited overlay-type tokens, distinct from bg.skeleton's always-opaque fill.

skeleton.$description: New token (2026-08-16), added for Skeleton alongside the light-mode fix (see that theme's own description for the full rationale) — dark mode's existing gray.900 value (vs bg.surface/gray.800 = 1.40:1) was already visibly correct, confirmed live in Storybook, so this was originally a rename onto a dedicated token, not a value change. Light mode was revised same day to a brand-tinted purple.200/emerald.200; dark mode deliberately stayed neutral gray rather than following suit, mirroring bg.brand-subtle's own precedent of dropping the brand tint entirely in dark mode. Moved from gray.900 to gray.950 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass, alongside the primitive gray.950 hex itself changing (#16151C → #24222A, at explicit direction, so this and its other existing consumer, border.default, land at a value the same pass judged correct rather than the prior near-black one). Skeleton hosts no text (decorative/aria-hidden, exempt from WCAG contrast requirements), but this token's whole reason for existing was *functional* visibility, not compliance — the original gray.50-reuse bug it replaced measured 1.04:1 against bg.surface, functionally invisible. Against the new bg.surface (gray.900), this lands at 1.11:1 — barely better than that original problem, a real trade-off knowingly accepted given this pass's explicit goal (a darker, more monochromatic dark theme), not an oversight. Revisit if Skeleton's dark-mode placeholder ever reads as genuinely too faint to serve its purpose.

surface.$description: Moved from gray.800 to gray.900 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction) as part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass — the user wanted dark mode to read noticeably darker overall, and bg.surface, as the representative background every token in this file is checked against by default, was the anchor for that. Every light-on-dark pairing only improves from a darker surface: text.primary 9.66:1 → 13.53:1, text.secondary 5.86:1 → 10.47:1, text.tertiary 4.34:1 → 8.21:1. Real side effects, not just improvements: (1) border.default (gray.950, unchanged since Phase 9 — a first draft of this note wrongly said gray.800 here, corrected 2026-09-06) narrows from bg.surface: 1.80:1 under the old gray.800 value, only 1.11:1 now — the opposite of a fix; this pass brings it most of the way back toward the exact Phase-9 problem it was created to escape, an accepted trade-off given this pass's own explicit goal (see border.default's own description). (1b) A genuine new collision this pass does introduce: border.neutral-subtle (gray.900, untouched) is now byte-identical to this token (1.00:1) — previously distinct at 1.40:1 against the old gray.800 value, and specifically the token docs.css's own table-border/divider rule was routed onto because it stayed distinct from border.default's own old collision with bg.surface. That workaround now collides with bg.surface itself instead — confirmed live, not assumed: docs.css's h2/table-border rules genuinely had no visible border in dark mode (checked on Code's own Docs page). Fixed the same day by flipping docs.css's three affected rules back to border.default — see docs.css's own comments for the full three-flip history. (2) bg.canvas (gray.700, unchanged) now reads 2.05:1 from this token instead of 1.46:1 — canvas already deliberately read *lighter* than surface as an intentional, narrow-purpose inversion (see bg.canvas's own description); this widens that gap further, still the same direction, not a new problem. (3) bg.scrim moved to gray.900 in the same pass (see that token's own description) — the two are now byte-identical again, continuing the established "scrim matches whatever bg.surface resolves to" pattern that already existed at the old gray.800 value.

brand.$description: Dark value moved emerald.500 → emerald.300 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — same fix already shipped for bg.neutral (Phase 34) and bg.danger/warning/success/info (2026-08-20 consolidation): a lighter dark-mode fill paired with dark text, instead of a mid-tone fill paired with white/near-white text. emerald.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 6.07:1 (fill/dot distinguishability, was 4.63:1 on the old emerald.500). Also absorbs the retired bg.brand-indicator (2026-08-21) — that token existed as a lighter step than bg.brand specifically because bg.brand's own old dark value didn't clear 3:1 well enough for a standalone dot (4.63:1); the new emerald.300 clears it more comfortably than the old indicator token itself did, so the separate token is no longer needed — every consumer (Badge's dot mode) now uses this token directly.

brand-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.brand. Dark value changed to emerald.200 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — one step lighter than the new bg.brand dark value, matching the X.300→X.200 dark-mode hover direction every other consolidated tone already uses (bg.danger red.300→red.200, bg.neutral gray.300→gray.200, etc.). text.on-brand (gray.900) on emerald.200 = 10.55:1, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin. Also resolves a pre-existing inconsistency: purple-dark's hover used to go darker (purple.500→purple.600) while emerald-dark's went lighter (emerald.500→emerald.400) — both brands now use the same lighten-in-dark-mode direction.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from gray.900 to gray.950 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), mirroring the same change on purple-dark — see that file's own description for the full rationale (part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode pass; moved darker rather than following bg.surface's own move to gray.900, specifically to keep this token's own text.brand/icon.brand pairings comfortable once bg.brand-subtle-hover deliberately stayed at gray.800). text.brand (emerald.400) on gray.950 measures 7.22:1 (was 4.63:1 vs the old gray.900); icon.brand (emerald.300) measures 9.47:1 (was 6.07:1). Same accepted trade-off as purple-dark's own description: gray.950 is now shared with border.default (unchanged, already gray.950 since Phase 9) and bg.skeleton, and this token sits at only ~1.1:1 against the new bg.surface — accepted given this pass's explicit goal of a darker, more monochromatic dark theme. Separately, border.neutral-subtle (gray.900, untouched by this pass) is now byte-identical to the new bg.surface (also gray.900, 1.00:1) — a genuine new collision that was not inert: it broke docs.css's own h2/table-border rules (confirmed live, no visible border), fixed the same day by flipping those rules to border.default instead; see bg.surface's own description and docs.css's own comments for the full history.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — one step lighter than brand-subtle (gray.900), matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction, same as purple-dark.json's own bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.link (emerald.400) on gray.800 = 4.63:1, passes AA (the tightest of the 12 new hover pairings verified for this change, still clear of the 4.5:1 floor).

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.500 to red.300, one step lighter. Old value measured only 2.90:1 against dark bg.surface, an outright WCAG 1.4.11 failure for a small standalone graphic (this is what bg.danger-indicator, now retired, existed to work around). red.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.67:1. text.on-danger moves to red.900 alongside this change (8.22:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.danger description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.danger now all resolve to this same step per mode).

danger-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.400 to red.200, alongside bg.danger's own dark move (red.500 → red.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-danger (red.900 as of this change) on red.200 = 10.68:1.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.900 to red.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's red.100 → red.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.danger (red.300) on red.950 = 10.32:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.22:1 on red.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.danger (red.300) on red.900 = 8.22:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.danger surface (the primary action inside a solid danger Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.danger: 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark. The fill against bg.danger itself is 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.500 to amber.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.05:1 against dark bg.surface — technically cleared WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor but with almost no margin (this is what bg.warning-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). amber.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.80:1. text.on-warning moves to amber.900 alongside this change (8.19:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.warning description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.warning now all resolve to this same step per mode).

warning-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.400 to amber.200, alongside bg.warning's own dark move (amber.500 → amber.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-warning (amber.900 as of this change) on amber.200 = 10.54:1.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.900 to amber.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's amber.100 → amber.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.950 = 10.44:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on amber.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.warning surface (the primary action inside a solid warning Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.warning: 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark. The fill against bg.warning itself is 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.500 to green.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.28:1 against dark bg.surface — a real pass, but thinner than desired for a dedicated indicator use (this is what bg.success-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). green.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 6.01:1. text.on-success moves to green.900 alongside this change (8.19:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.success description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.success now all resolve to this same step per mode).

success-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.400 to green.200, alongside bg.success's own dark move (green.500 → green.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-success (green.900 as of this change) on green.200 = 10.32:1.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.900 to green.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's green.100 → green.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.success (green.300) on green.950 = 10.68:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on green.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.success (green.300) on green.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation.

on-success.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.success surface (the primary action inside a solid success Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-success (white light / green.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.success: 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark. The fill against bg.success itself is 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.500 to blue.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.09:1 against dark bg.surface — a real pass, but thinner than desired for a dedicated indicator use (this is what bg.info-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). blue.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.85:1. text.on-info moves to blue.900 alongside this change (8.20:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.info description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.info now all resolve to this same step per mode).

info-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.400 to blue.200, alongside bg.info's own dark move (blue.500 → blue.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-info (blue.900 as of this change) on blue.200 = 10.46:1.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.900 to blue.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's blue.100 → blue.50 (2026-07-27), preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.info (blue.300) on blue.950 = 10.51:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.20:1 on blue.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint. Dark mode has no equivalent to light mode's razor-edge margin (see purple-light.json's own bg.info-subtle description) — text.info's dark value was already blue.300 before and after, so nothing changed here.

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.info (blue.300) on blue.900 = 8.20:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation.

on-info.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.info surface (the primary action inside a solid info Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-info (white light / blue.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.info: 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark. The fill against bg.info itself is 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

highlight.$description: New token family (2026-10-04), the general highlight and accent colour on the new yellow scale, shared across both brands and not a status tone. Dark: yellow.300, 8.97:1 vs bg.surface; text.on-highlight (yellow.900) on it is 6.42:1.

highlight-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.highlight. Dark yellow.200: text.on-highlight (yellow.900) on it is 7.63:1.

highlight-subtle.$description: Light highlight tint, the marker behind highlighted text and the fill of a subtle highlight badge. Dark yellow.950: text.highlight (yellow.300) on it is 9.08:1. Sits at about 1.01:1 against bg.surface, a deliberate decorative tint like the other dark subtle fills.

highlight-subtle-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.highlight-subtle. Dark yellow.900: text.highlight (yellow.300) on it is 6.42:1.

on-highlight.$description: Inverted fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.highlight surface, the same value as text.on-highlight, its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill. yellow.900 on bg.highlight is 6.42:1.

neutral.$description: Merged with the retired bg.neutral (gray.500, offline/dot-only fill) and renamed from bg.neutral-strong (2026-08-21). Dark value moved gray.600 → gray.300 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — gray.600 alone couldn't satisfy both real uses in dark mode (2.14:1 as a dot against bg.surface, failing 3:1). Fixed the same way bg.danger/warning/success/info were already fixed in the 2026-08-20 consolidation: switch to a lighter dark-mode fill paired with dark (not white) text, rather than try to keep one gray working for both a light-on-dark dot and a dark-on-light text fill. gray.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 5.86:1 (dot use, clears 3:1 with a wide margin, better than the original bg.neutral's own 3.10:1); text.on-neutral's own dark value moved white → gray.900 in the same pass (see that token's own description), giving gray.900-on-gray.300 = 8.21:1 (text use, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin). Real, visible change for Badge.solidNeutral/Tag.solidNeutral/Tag.selected.outlineNeutral/Tooltip in dark mode — dark text instead of white, not just a number — confirmed live before considering this done.

neutral-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.neutral-strong-hover (2026-08-21), hover state of bg.neutral (formerly bg.neutral-strong). Dark value moved gray.700 → gray.200 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — same fix as bg.neutral's own dark value (see that token's description): one step lighter than the new gray.300 base, matching the X.300→X.200 dark-mode hover direction every other tone's own solid fill already uses (e.g. bg.danger red.300→red.200). gray.200 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 7.47:1; text.on-neutral's new dark value (gray.900) on gray.200 = 10.47:1 — both comfortably clear their floors.

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here instead of sitting up near bg.canvas/bg.surface — no value change at the time. Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent", value moved from gray.800 to gray.900 in the same edit. Moved back to gray.800 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass — bg.surface itself moved to gray.900 in the same pass (see its own description), and re-verification against that new, darker representative background left plenty of room to bring this token back down a step: text.secondary (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral) now measures 7.47:1 (was 8.21:1 against the old gray.900, still comfortably clear of AA), text.primary 9.66:1 (was 13.53:1), text.tertiary/icon.default 5.86:1 (was 8.21:1, icon.default shares text.tertiary's own primitive step — see that token's own description, verified 2026-09-04 finalizing Image). All three stay well clear of their respective floors despite the tightening. Real trade-off: now shares gray.800 with bg.track, bg.code, and bg.brand-subtle-hover (unchanged) — four conceptually distinct tokens at one value, none of which are typically adjacent in real usage, an accepted overlap given this pass's explicit darker/more-monochromatic goal (same class of trade-off already accepted elsewhere in this file, e.g. the former bg.subtle/bg.surface-raised collision). No longer collides with border.neutral-subtle (that token stayed at gray.900 before this pass and is now gray.950, see its own description — the two were flagged as an accepted, low-priority overlap previously and are no longer even the same value).

neutral-subtle-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle-hover (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here — no value change at the time. Originally added 2026-08-17, found adding Tag's whole-tag clickable/selectable mode — bg.neutral-subtle's own hover step, one primitive scale step lighter than whatever bg.neutral-subtle itself currently is (the dark-mode hover direction bg.brand-subtle-hover/etc. already use). Moved from gray.800 to gray.700 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass — bg.neutral-subtle itself moved from gray.900 to gray.800 in the same pass (see its own description), so this hover step moved down with it to preserve the one-step-lighter-on-hover relationship (rest gray.800 → hover gray.700, same 1-step gap as before, just both shifted one step darker together). text.secondary (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral's own paired text) on the new gray.700 measures 5.10:1 (was 7.47:1 against the old gray.800) — tighter, but still comfortably clears the 4.5:1 AA floor. No longer byte-identical to bg.surface (that token moved to gray.900 in the same pass) — now shares gray.700 with bg.canvas instead, a new, harmless collision of the same accepted class (nothing pairs the two directly).

on-neutral.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.neutral surface (the primary action inside a solid neutral Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-neutral (white light / gray.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.secondary: 6.88:1 light / 10.47:1 dark. The fill against bg.neutral itself is 4.70:1 light / 8.21:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

track.$description: New token (2026-08-22), added for ProgressBar's empty/unfilled track — was reusing bg.neutral-subtle, the same 'existing token reused for an unverified new purpose' bug that led to bg.skeleton (Phase 18). Dark value originally carried over unchanged from bg.neutral-subtle (gray.900, 1.40:1 vs the then-current bg.surface). Moved to gray.800 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass — bg.neutral-subtle itself (this token's original source value) moved to gray.800 in the same pass, and bg.surface moved to gray.900, so this token followed suit rather than being left stranded on the old value. Still measured 1.40:1 against the new bg.surface at that point — still failing the 3:1 non-text floor WCAG 1.4.11 asks for graphical objects required to understand content, still accepted at explicit user direction for the same reason as the light-mode value (see purple-light.json/emerald-light.json for the full rationale) — a deliberate, informed exception, not a verified pass. Brand-agnostic. **Moved again to gray.700 (2026-09-15, at explicit direction)** — measures 2.05:1 against bg.surface (gray.900), still short of 3:1 but a real step up from 1.40:1, matching the same-day light-mode bump (gray.100 → gray.200, see that value's own description) rather than leaving dark mode disproportionately fainter. No longer shares its exact value with bg.neutral-subtle/bg.code/bg.brand-subtle-hover (all still gray.800). Revisit with gray.500 (3.25:1 against bg.surface dark) or gray.400 (4.34:1) if this needs to actually clear 3:1 later.

track-strong.$description: New token (2026-08-30), added for Switch's unchecked-state track fill — was reusing bg.neutral-subtle, the exact 'existing token reused for an unverified new purpose' bug already fixed twice (bg.skeleton, Phase 18; bg.track, above). Dark value requested as gray.900 initially — checked directly against bg.surface (gray.800) and found to measure only 1.4:1, reproducing the same near-invisible defect in dark mode instead of fixing it, so gray.400 was used instead: 4.34:1 vs bg.surface, the same already-verified value border.neutral-strong (Phase 23) established for this identical 'needs to read as a real UI boundary in dark mode' case. Brand-agnostic. **Moved to gray.600 (2026-09-15, at explicit direction)** — Switch's own *resting* unchecked state no longer consumes this token (moved to bg.track, see ADR-0016), leaving Indicators' inactive-dot fill as its resting-state consumer; measures ~3.00:1 against bg.surface (gray.900) — right at the 3:1 non-text floor, a razor-thin pass rather than gray.400's comfortable 4.34:1 margin, worth re-measuring if the primitive scale or bg.surface itself is ever regenerated. **Also reused, same day, at explicit direction, for Switch's own unchecked-hover state** — replacing bg.neutral there (gray.600 light / gray.300 dark, 3.25:1/8.21:1), which had been this token's own hover-state pairing back when this token was Switch's resting color. Since Switch's resting state is now bg.track (gray.700 dark), the hover step to this token (gray.600, one primitive step) reads as a clear, perceptible lightening — confirmed via computed style (`rgb(91,88,107)` → `rgb(117,113,135)`) and live screenshot, not just computed.

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.950 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction — code pill drops the blue tint in dark mode specifically, moving to a neutral gray fill instead. Light mode is unchanged (blue.50). Moved again, from gray.700 to gray.800 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), part of a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass covering several bg.* tokens at once. text.secondary on the new value measures 7.47:1 (was 5.10:1 against the old gray.700) — a real improvement. **Real side effect, not carried through this pass**: border.code's own dark value stayed at gray.700 (not part of this pass's token list), so the two are no longer byte-identical — previously the pill's border was deliberately invisible against its own fill (an explicit flat/borderless dark-mode treatment, not an oversight, see border.code's own description); now they diverge at 1.46:1, so the border becomes visibly present in dark mode where it previously wasn't. Flagged as a real, visible consequence of this change, not silently absorbed — revisit border.code's own dark value if the flat/borderless look is still wanted. Retired 2026-08-20 in favor of bg.info-subtle directly, restored the same day, reversing that retirement. Adopted by the real Code.tsx atom (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, during its own review pass, earlier the same day as this token's own value change) — see that token's own light-mode description.

code-highlight.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s highlighted lines. gray.800 (the same value as `bg.code`), a step lighter than the block (`bg.code-block`, gray.900), so a highlighted line reads as emphasised. A band lighter still cannot work in dark mode: every syntax colour falls to 3.6–4.1:1 on gray.700. Every `text.syntax-*` colour clears 4.5:1 on it (5.3:1 or more), and so does `text.secondary`, which the line numbers use.

code-block.$description: New token (2026-09-26), the background of `CodeBlock`. gray.900 in dark mode, a step darker than `bg.code` (gray.800), the inline pill's fill — so that a highlighted line (`bg.code-highlight`, gray.800) is the *lighter* band, as an emphasised line reads, while every syntax colour still clears 4.5:1 on both (7.4:1 or more on the block, 5.3:1 or more on the band). Equal to `bg.surface` in this theme, so a block is set apart from the page by its border, `border.code` (gray.700). Every `text.syntax-*` colour and `text.secondary` (line numbers, the title) is measured against it.

secondary.$description: Moved from gray.300 to gray.200 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, driven by bg.canvas's move to gray.700 the same day: text.secondary on bg.canvas measured 4.00:1 on gray.300 (fails the 4.5:1 AA text floor), gray.200 clears it at 5.10:1. Also improves against every other bg.* pairing: 7.47:1 on bg.surface (was 5.86:1 on gray.300), 10.47:1 on bg.subtle (was 8.21:1).

tertiary.$description: Moved from gray.400 to gray.300 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, same motivation as text.secondary's move above. Still doesn't fully clear the 4.5:1 text floor against bg.canvas (gray.300 on gray.700 measures 4.00:1) — it does clear the 3:1 non-text floor there, but this token's own literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder) need 4.5:1, same standard that ruled out gray.500 originally (see history below). No primitive step between 300 and 400 exists to close that last gap without also moving past text.secondary's own gray.200. Given that, `bg.canvas` should never host `text.tertiary` literal text — enforced by guideline note (see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md) rather than by chasing a lighter value here, since 5.86:1 on bg.surface and 8.21:1 on bg.subtle (this token's actual intended surfaces) are both comfortably clear at gray.300. History: gray.500 originally failed AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses; gray.400 gave 6.08:1 against the surfaces it was verified on at the time (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

on-brand.$description: Text/icons on a solid bg.brand fill. Dark value changed to gray.900 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction), replacing a per-brand split that had accumulated rather than been designed: purple-dark used white, emerald-dark used gray.950 (emerald.500 was too light for white text) — now both brand themes share one value, matching bg.brand's own dark value becoming brand-agnostic in relative terms (each brand's own tone.300 step). gray.900 on the new bg.brand dark = 8.51:1; on bg.brand-hover dark = 10.55:1 — both clear 4.5:1 with a wide margin, well past the old purple pairing's own 4.51:1 near-miss (white on purple.500).

on-danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to red.900, so a solid bg.danger fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic red surface (fill + text both red-family) rather than red fill + neutral-gray text. red.900 on bg.danger's own new dark value (red.300) = 8.22:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.22:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to blue.900, so a solid bg.info fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic blue surface (fill + text both blue-family) rather than blue fill + neutral-gray text. blue.900 on bg.info's own new dark value (blue.300) = 8.20:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.56:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to green.900, so a solid bg.success fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic green surface (fill + text both green-family) rather than green fill + neutral-gray text. green.900 on bg.success's own new dark value (green.300) = 8.19:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.91:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to amber.900, so a solid bg.warning fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic amber surface (fill + text both amber-family) rather than amber fill + neutral-gray text. amber.900 on bg.warning's own new dark value (amber.300) = 8.19:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.49:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral fill (Badge solid variant). Dark value moved white → gray.900 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — bg.neutral's own dark value moved gray.600 → gray.300 in the same pass (see that token's description) to fix a real 3:1 non-text-contrast failure on the dot use case; white text on the new lighter gray.300 would only measure 1.72:1, so dark mode switches to dark text instead, the same pattern text.on-danger/warning/success/info already use in dark mode (e.g. text.on-danger = red.900, not white). gray.900 on gray.300 = 8.21:1, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin.

on-highlight.$description: Text on a solid bg.highlight fill. yellow.900 on yellow.300: 6.42:1.

link.$description: Token update (2026-08-20), at explicit direction — moved off the brand anchor (was emerald.400 in this theme, purple.300 in the other) to a shared blue.300, now literally identical across both brand themes and both modes. De-brands link color entirely — see purple-light.json's own text.link description for the full rationale, including the two real consumers (Avatar's default fill, Storybook's own toolbar) moved to text.brand to preserve their previous appearance. blue.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 5.85:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 4.63:1 on the old emerald.400 — an improvement, and this theme's own tightest text.link margin before this change). Byte-identical to text.info's own dark value as a direct consequence.

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links. Originally reused text.link's own resolved value; text.link was de-branded to a shared blue (2026-08-20, see that token's own description), so this token now stands on its own — value unchanged, still emerald.400. emerald.600 (the literal brand anchor) on bg.surface (gray.800) is only 2.42:1, failing AA — emerald.400 gives 4.63:1, freshly re-verified (2026-08-20); an earlier recorded figure of 3.39:1 here had been computed against a stale gray.900 value predating Phase 9's bg.surface revert and was never corrected until now.

danger.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation (already red.300) — now also the shared value bg.danger, border.danger, and icon.danger resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.danger description for the consolidation this is part of.

warning.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation (already amber.300) — now also the shared value bg.warning, border.warning, and icon.warning resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.warning description for the consolidation this is part of.

success.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation (already green.300) — now also the shared value bg.success, border.success, and icon.success resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.success description for the consolidation this is part of.

info.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation (already blue.300) — now also the shared value bg.info, border.info, and icon.info resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.info description for the consolidation this is part of.

highlight.$description: New token family (2026-10-04), the general highlight and accent colour on the new yellow scale, shared across both brands and not a status tone. Dark yellow.300: 8.97:1 vs bg.surface, 6.42:1 on bg.highlight-subtle-hover.

syntax-keyword.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — keywords and at-rules (`const`, `if`, `@media`). purple.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.3:1 — AA.

syntax-string.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — string literals. green.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.0:1 — AA.

syntax-number.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — numbers, units and the literals `true`, `false`, `null`. amber.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.8:1 — AA.

syntax-function.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — function and command names at a call. blue.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.9:1 — AA.

syntax-type.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — type and class names (`Promise`, `Button`). emerald.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.1:1 — AA.

syntax-property.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — object keys, CSS properties and HTML/JSX attribute names. blue.200 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 7.5:1 — AA.

syntax-tag.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — HTML/JSX tag names. red.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.7:1 — AA.

syntax-comment.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — comments — muted by hue, not by contrast, so it still clears AA. gray.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.9:1 — AA.

syntax-inserted.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — an added line in a diff. green.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.0:1 — AA.

syntax-deleted.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — a removed line in a diff. red.300 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.7:1 — AA.

white.$description: White in all 4 themes and both modes, for text drawn on a surface that is dark in every theme (the ImageViewer stage over bg.overlay). Shares the reasoning of icon.white: bg.overlay stays neutral.black in dark mode, so a text token that flipped dark would be invisible there. Not for text on a themed surface: use text.primary or text.on-* there. Like bg.overlay, no fixed WCAG pairing (what is behind the scrim is arbitrary); white on bg.overlay at opacity.80 over the whitest content is 12.6:1.

default.$description: Moved from gray.800 to gray.950 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, to fix an exact-collision with bg.surface at the time (both gray.800). Moved again to gray.900 (2026-09-06, still within the same darker-dark-mode retuning pass, at explicit direction) as an intermediate step when the gray.950 primitive's own hex changed and bg.surface separately moved to gray.900 — narrowed this token's own escape from that collision back down to 1.11:1 (from 1.80:1), an accepted trade-off at the time. **Moved a third time, to gray.800 (2026-09-06, later the same day, at explicit direction)** — real component-hosting surfaces (Input/Textarea/Select/Kbd/Divider all use this token) needed a properly re-verified value, not just whatever the gray.950 hex change happened to leave behind. Net effect against this token's actual real-world pairings: vs bg.surface (gray.900) = 1.40:1 (up from the intermediate 1.11:1 — a real improvement, not just a return to the original 1.80:1, since bg.surface itself is darker now than when this token first moved to escape gray.800); vs bg.canvas (gray.700, unchanged) = 1.46:1 (down from 2.28:1 — canvas got relatively closer now that this token sits one step lighter); vs bg.neutral-subtle (gray.800, unchanged since the same day's earlier pass) = **1.00:1, byte-identical** — a new, accepted collision (this token and bg.neutral-subtle are conceptually distinct — a border vs. a fill — and not typically drawn directly against each other in real component usage, but flagged here rather than left undocumented). Still fails the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor against all of these real surfaces either way — a pre-existing gap, not created or worsened by any of these moves; this token is decorative, not state-identifying, so 1.4.11 doesn't actually bind it (see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md).

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.subtle (2026-08-21), same border.* rotation as the light file (see border.neutral-subtle's own light-mode description for the full four-way mapping). Dark counterpart, value unchanged (gray.900) at the time. Moved to gray.950 (2026-09-06, at explicit direction), swapping values with border.default (which moved the other way, gray.950 → gray.800, in the same session — see that token's own description for the fuller history). This token is decorative, Storybook-chrome only — no shipped component consumes it directly — so this move doesn't affect any real component. It does, however, matter for docs.css: `docs.css`'s own h2/table-border rules were flipped earlier the same day from this token to border.default, specifically because this token had become byte-identical to bg.surface (both gray.900) — now that this token is gray.950 instead, it's clear of that collision again (1.11:1 against bg.surface), but docs.css already points at border.default (now gray.800, 1.40:1 against bg.surface, an even better result) and there's no reason to flip it back — re-verify against bg.surface's actual value before touching either token again, since this pair has now flipped/swapped multiple times (see docs.css's own comments for the full history).

neutral.$description: Renamed from border.strong (2026-08-21), same border.* rotation (see the light-mode border.neutral's own description). Dark counterpart, value unchanged (gray.600) — the default resting border on Checkbox/Kbd, hover-state border on Select/Input/Textarea/Button's secondary variant/IconButton/Indicators, same as light. Blockquote moved off this token onto border.brand instead (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, during its own review pass) — see that token's own description.

neutral-strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral (2026-08-21), part of the border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). Dark counterpart to border.neutral-strong (light) — see that token's own description for its purpose (and why it isn't the one Tag's outline variant actually consumes). Doesn't reuse the token now named border.neutral's own dark value (gray.600, only 2.14:1 against dark bg.surface — well under 3:1) for the same reason the light value doesn't. gray.400 vs bg.surface (dark) = 4.34:1, a comfortable margin.

on-neutral.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.neutral surface (the secondary action inside a solid neutral Alert). Same value as text.on-neutral (white light / gray.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.neutral: 4.70:1 light / 8.21:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral-strong (2026-08-21), part of the border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). Dark counterpart to border.strong (light) — found adding Tag's selectable solid-variant ring. Reuses the same primitive step text.secondary already uses in dark mode (gray.200), independently tracked. gray.200 vs bg.surface (dark) = 7.47:1. Now consumed directly by Tag's outline/selected-solid-neutral rings (Tag.module.css).

brand.$description: Dark value changed emerald.400 → emerald.300 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction), matching bg.brand's own dark value now that both are the same tone.300 step — previously border.brand reused border.focus's dark value instead of bg.brand's own (see Phase 22), since bg.brand's old dark step measured only 2.24:1/3.41:1 against dark bg.surface, too weak for a real border. That workaround is no longer needed: emerald.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 6.07:1, up from 4.63:1 on the old emerald.400 — a real improvement, not just a rename. Second consumer: Blockquote's default-variant accent border (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, moved off border.neutral — see that token's own description).

brand-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.brand (2026-08-20), for naming consistency with its sibling family tokens (border.danger-subtle/warning-subtle/success-subtle/info-subtle all carry the -subtle suffix for the same decorative-only role; this one hadn't, despite being the exact same kind of token). Value unchanged. Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from emerald.400). Dark value moved off the literal emerald.100 shared with light mode to emerald.900 (2026-08-16, mirroring the same change on purple-dark — see that file's own description) — emerald.100 on bg.brand-subtle (gray.900) measured 12.46:1, a stark high-contrast ring that read nothing like light mode's own low-key accent. emerald.900 on gray.900 is 1.08:1, mirroring light mode's own 1.09:1 (emerald.100 on emerald.50) — both intentionally subtle. This token is for decorative UI accents, not a border that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply here (border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying).

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.400 to red.300, absorbing border.danger-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer now uses this token directly) and matching bg.danger/text.danger/icon.danger's shared dark step. red.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.67:1, an improvement over the previous 4.13:1. See purple-light.json's own border.danger description for the consolidation this is part of.

danger-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, dark counterpart to border.danger-subtle (light) — follows the same emerald.900-in-dark-mode pattern established for border.brand-subtle above. Not neutralized to a shared gray the way border.brand-subtle's dark value is: family accents keep their own tint in dark mode (bg.danger-subtle here is red.950, not gray.900 — see that token's own description). Pairs with bg.danger-subtle for any component's danger-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component — first used by Avatar's `colorful` danger variant (2026-08-16), but not scoped to it. red.900 on red.950 is 1.26:1, comparably subtle to border.brand-subtle's own 1.08:1 dark pairing. Brand-agnostic — identical value in every brand theme. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.danger surface (the secondary action inside a solid danger Alert). Same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.danger: 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.400 to amber.300, absorbing border.warning-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer now uses this token directly) and matching bg.warning/text.warning/icon.warning's shared dark step. amber.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.80:1, an improvement over the previous 4.31:1. See purple-light.json's own border.warning description for the consolidation this is part of.

warning-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.warning-subtle for any component's warning-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. amber.900 on amber.950 is 1.27:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.warning surface (the secondary action inside a solid warning Alert). Same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.warning: 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.400 to green.300, absorbing border.success-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer now uses this token directly) and matching bg.success/text.success/icon.success's shared dark step. green.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 6.01:1, an improvement over the previous 4.57:1. See purple-light.json's own border.success description for the consolidation this is part of.

success-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.success-subtle for any component's success-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. green.900 on green.950 is 1.30:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-success.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.success surface (the secondary action inside a solid success Alert). Same value as text.on-success (white light / green.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.success: 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.400 to blue.300, absorbing border.info-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer now uses this token directly) and matching bg.info/text.info/icon.info's shared dark step. blue.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.85:1, an improvement over the previous 4.35:1. See purple-light.json's own border.info description for the consolidation this is part of.

info-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.info-subtle for any component's info-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. blue.900 on blue.950 is 1.28:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-info.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.info surface (the secondary action inside a solid info Alert). Same value as text.on-info (white light / blue.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.info: 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

highlight.$description: State-identifying highlight border. Dark yellow.300: 8.97:1 vs bg.surface.

highlight-subtle.$description: Decorative highlight-tinted ring, around bg.highlight-subtle. Dark yellow.900, about 1.4:1, a deliberate exception like the other subtle borders.

on-highlight.$description: Outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.highlight surface, the same value as text.on-highlight, its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border.

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.900 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, matching bg.code's own move to gray.700 in dark mode at the time — the two were byte-identical there, an explicit flat/borderless pill treatment for dark mode specifically (light mode keeps the blue.100/blue.50 pairing and its visible border, unchanged). Briefly paired with bg.info-subtle instead (2026-08-20, when bg.code was retired) and measured 2.63:1 against that fill; bg.code was restored the same day, reversing that retirement, so this token went back to its original byte-identical-with-bg.code dark treatment. Original description: paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand-subtle. Adopted by the real Code.tsx atom alongside bg.code (2026-09-06, at explicit direction). Later the same day, bg.code moved to gray.800 (a coordinated darker-dark-mode retuning pass) while this token stayed at gray.700 — briefly broke the flat/borderless pairing (1.46:1 apart, a visible border where there wasn't one). Moved to gray.800 later the same day, at explicit direction, to restore the byte-identical flat treatment. **Moved back to gray.700 (2026-09-06, later still the same day, at explicit direction)** — deliberately re-diverges from bg.code (gray.800): the pill now has a visibly present border again (1.46:1 apart) rather than the flat/borderless look, a knowing choice this time, not a side effect. Still under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor, still decorative/not state-identifying, so no compliance concern either way.

white.$description: White in all 4 themes and both modes, for a border or focus ring drawn on a surface that is dark in every theme (the ImageViewer stage's focus ring and current-thumbnail border). Shares the reasoning of icon.white and text.white. Not for a border on a themed surface: use border.default, border.focus or the border.on-* family there.

default.$description: Mapped to gray.200 (2026-10-18, at explicit direction; was gray.300), the same step as text.secondary, so a default icon and secondary text read at one strength, and no longer the step text.tertiary shares. Verified vs bg.surface: 10.47:1; vs bg.neutral-subtle: 7.47:1; vs bg.neutral-subtle-hover and bg.canvas: 5.10:1 — all clear the 3:1 non-text floor, and the 4.5:1 text one, comfortably. Also Image's fallback icon, its default state.

brand.$description: Moved from emerald.400 to emerald.300 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, mirroring the same change on purple-dark (see that file's own description for the full rationale: emerald.400 passed the 3:1 non-text floor against bg.surface but failed against bg.canvas). emerald.300 measures 6.07:1 on bg.surface, 4.15:1 on bg.canvas — both comfortably clear, the latter also clearing the stricter 4.5:1 text floor for headroom.

on-brand.$description: New token (2026-08-22), completing the icon and icon.on- pattern for brand — dark counterpart to icon.on-brand (light); see that token's own description. gray.900 on bg.brand's own dark value (purple.300/emerald.300) = 7.45:1/8.51:1.

white.$description: Renamed from icon.on-overlay (2026-09-05, at explicit direction — see the light file's own description for the full naming-exception reasoning). Dark counterpart to icon.white (light), except the value doesn't change: unlike every other icon.on-* pair, this one deliberately stays white in dark mode too, since bg.overlay itself stays neutral.black in dark mode (it doesn't lighten the way bg.neutral/bg.brand/etc. do).
